goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims a compile error because `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no args while `UsernamePasswordForm` defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`. These are different classes; a method defined in `UsernamePasswordForm` is irrelevant to whether `UsernameForm` compiles. The diff does not show whether `UsernameForm` already has (or inherits) a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` method, so the alleged compile error cannot be verified from the shown changes and the reasoning conflates two separate types.

adjudication.rationale: In the modified tests (e.g., PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest and other updated test files), assertions like `assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), notNullValue())` don’t add meaningful verification beyond “the call didn’t throw”, because Selenium `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when the element is absent rather than returning null. So the matcher itself is tautological; the test would fail the same way without `notNullValue()` if the element is missing. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue, not a product bug.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces `import static org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.browser.AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;` in `AuthenticatorUtils` and adds `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError()` that reads that auth note. To enable this, the constant in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` is changed from `protected` to `public`. This is a concrete new coupling from a generic util (`...authenticators.util`) to a browser-flow-specific authenticator class/constant, matching the finding’s dependency-direction concern. It’s an architecture/scope issue rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm` returning `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;`. Call sites then use `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`. The method name reads like a feature/policy check, but it also encodes the separate precondition "user is present", so understanding why the user-null check matters requires reading the implementation. This is a clarity/intent issue (naming/API semantics), not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UsernameForm.authenticate()` is changed to call `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but none of the modified classes in this PR add or expose a zero-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` method for `UsernameForm` (the only newly added helper is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which is a different class and signature). adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 — USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` was widened from `protected` to `public`, expanding which code outside the authenticator hierarchy can read/rely on this re-authentication auth-note key, increasing coupling/attack surface for any future misuse even though no current misuse was found.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `protected static final` to `public static final` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`. This enables access from `AuthenticatorUtils` (in a different package) via `import static ...USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`, which would not compile with `protected` visibility. While not a direct functional/security defect shown by the diff, it does concretely widen the API surface and increases coupling by making an internal auth-note key publicly consumable by any code.
